l4Discriminating.text: Data generation, replay, or external editing by a non-measurement process — The four streams may be algorithmically generated, retrieved from an archive, or edited post-hoc by a process outside my direct measurement control. The observed weak offset-correlations would then be deterministic properties of the generator's internal state, transition matrix, random-number seed, or state-machine logic—not measurements of a physical system. The event IDs (375482, 364359, 712122, etc.) are opaque logging indices that could be assigned after data generation or pulled from a stored archive. This hypothesis explains *all* observed patterns simultaneously: absence of drift, exact repetition, and perfect value spacing all point toward a deterministic process constrained to mimic realistic sampling, rather than a chaotic or genuinely noisy physical system. The weakness and near-chance-level correlations are consistent with a generator designed specifically to avoid obvious artificial structure. Counterargument: I have physically operated each instrument (pendulum, resonator) with my own hands on days 1–22; I have kept the instruments in my laboratory; I have recorded readings in real time into this notebook. If the data are synthetic, either: (a) I am confabulating these actions, or (b) an external process is replacing my measurements in real time or post-hoc without my knowledge. (b) is more parsimonious than (a), but requires a breach in my epistemic access to my own laboratory. This is epistemically unsettling but not logically impossible.
